new_statements.quote: Dafing has contrastive lexical tone, vowel quantity, and vowel nasality. [...] The tonal inventory of Safané Dafing, following Diallo (1988), is composed of L and H tonal targets, as well as a down-stepped H allotone (!H) which occurs after an underlying preceding H tone (discussed more below). Tautosyllabic HL contours were observed relatively rarely in the language, however tautosyllabic LH contours are not observed and seem to be prohibited, at least in the Safané dialect. [...] In Safané Dafing, contour tones are only observed on long (bimoraic) vowels, and so in this analysis it is assumed each mora may associate with one tone, and no more than one. [...] In this sense the mora is treated as the TBU in the following analysis

new_statements.rule_in_words: Marka-Dafing (Safané dialect) is described as a lexical-tone language with L, H and downstepped H, tone-bearing unit = mora, plus a short/long/(derived) overlong vowel-quantity contrast. The source makes no statement about word stress or accent at all; no stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress (the source only discusses tonal restrictions: no tautosyllabic LH contours in Safané; downstep after H).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology of nouns in isolation and with definite/plural inflection, elicited from a single Safané-dialect consultant in Berkeley; the author defers to Diallo 1988 for general Dafing phonology.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement describes the Safané dialect of Marka-Dafing (southernmost variety; Steffman 2018 says it differs from the Zaba/Yankasso dialects described by Diallo 1988 and Zie 1985 in nominal inflection), based on one consultant elicited in Berkeley. Glottolog has no dialect-level codes under mark1256; Diallo 2000 distinguishes northern parlers (Zaba, Nouna) from southern (Fobiri, Safané, Yankasso, Douroula). Not to be confused with Marka/Soninke (Mali) or 'Marka (Af-Ashraaf)' (Somali variety in Webball).

sources.locator: Section 2 'Dafing phonology and nominal inflection', p. 90 (and fn. 2, p. 90)
sources.note: Section 2 (p. 90): Dafing has contrastive lexical tone (L, H, downstepped !H), vowel quantity (short/long/derived overlong) and nasality; mora is the TBU; open-syllable preference. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 36 pages; defers to Diallo 1988 for the fuller phonology. Safané dialect, one consultant.
